docs.title: FlavorPack
docs.text: Progressive Secure Package Format (PSPF/2025) - A cross-language packaging system for creating self-contained, portable executables.

docs.title: What is FlavorPack?
docs.text: FlavorPack is a packaging system that creates single-file executables from Python applications. No installation, no dependencies, no configuration required.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Create a package
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --output myapp.psp

# Run the package  
./myapp.psp

docs.title: Package Command
docs.text:
flavor pack [OPTIONS]

Options: - --manifest PATH - Manifest file (pyproject.toml or JSON) - --output PATH - Output file path - --launcher-bin PATH - Launcher binary to use - --builder-bin PATH - Builder binary to use - --key-seed TEXT - Seed for deterministic keys - --platform TEXT - Target platform - --strip - Strip debug symbols - --compress - Compression level (0-9)

Examples: 

# Basic package
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --output myapp.psp

# Deterministic build
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --output myapp.psp --key-seed production-v1

# Custom launcher
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --output myapp.psp --launcher-bin ingredients/bin/flavor-go-launcher-darwin_arm64

docs.text:

docs.title: Inspect Command

docs.text:

# Read package metadata
reader = PSPFReader("myapp.psp")

docs.title: Working with Slots

reader = PSPFReader("myapp.psp")

docs.title: Ed25519 Signatures
docs.text: All packages are signed with Ed25519: - 32-byte public key stored at index offset 64-95 - 512-byte signature stored at index offset 128-639 - Signs the index block (with signature zeroed) and metadata - Verified on every launch unless FLAVOR_INSECURE=1

docs.title: Key Generation
docs.text:
from flavor.psp.format_2025.crypto import generate_keypair

# Deterministic keys from seed
private_key, public_key = generate_keypair(seed="my-seed")

# Random keys
private_key, public_key = generate_keypair()

docs.title: Verification Process
docs.text:
1. Read public key from index block
  2. Read signature from index block
  3. Zero out signature field in index copy
  4. Concatenate index and metadata
  5. Verify Ed25519 signature
  6. Reject if verification fails

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: FlavorPack is a multi-language packaging system implementing the Progressive Secure Package Format (PSPF/2025). It creates self-extracting, polyglot archives that are simultaneously: - Native OS executables (Linux/macOS/Windows) - PSPF packages with cryptographic integrity verification - Python-installable packages with embedded dependencies

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Python Orchestrator                      │
│                    (src/flavor/packaging/)                   │
│  • High-level packaging logic                                │
│  • Manifest processing                                       │
│  • Dependency resolution                                     │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                 │                        │
        ┌────────▼────────┐      ┌───────▼────────┐
        │   Go Ingredients │      │  Rust Ingredients│
        │(ingredients/flavor-go)│ (ingredients/flavor-rs)
        │ • Builder       │      │ • Builder      │
        │ • Launcher      │      │ • Launcher     │
        └─────────────────┘      └────────────────┘
                 │                        │
        ┌────────▼────────────────────────▼────────┐
        │          PSPF Package (.psp file)        │
        │  • Native launcher (platform-specific)   │
        │  • Metadata block (gzipped JSON)         │
        │  • Slot table                            │
        │  • Slot data (tar.gz archives)           │
        │  • Magic trailer (8200 bytes)            │
        └───────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Ed25519 Signatures
docs.text:
• Every package is signed with Ed25519
  • 32-byte public key in index block
  • 512-byte signature field for integrity
  • Verification on every launch

docs.title: Checksum Validation
docs.text:
• Adler-32 for index block
  • SHA-256 for metadata
  • Adler-32 for each slot
  • All checksums verified before execution

docs.title: Secure Extraction
docs.text:
• Path traversal prevention
  • Permission preservation
  • Atomic file operations
  • Secure temporary directories

docs.title: Workenv Management
docs.text:
Packages extract to cached work environments:

Linux: ~/.cache/flavor/workenv/{name}_{version}/ macOS: ~/Library/Caches/flavor/workenv/{name}_{version}/ Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\flavor\workenv\{name}_{version}\

Features: - Persistent caching across runs - Checksum-based validation - Atomic directory creation - Automatic cleanup of old versions

docs.title: Slot System
docs.text:
Slots are numbered containers (0-based) for different components:

Slot Purpose Typical Content 0 Runtime Python environment 1 Application App code 2+ Resources Assets, configs

docs.title: Encoding Types
docs.text:
• RAW (0): Uncompressed data
  • TAR (1): Tar archive
  • GZIP (2): Gzipped file
  • TGZ (3): Tar + gzip

docs.title: Lifecycle Types
docs.text:
• RUNTIME (2): Extract on every run
  • CACHE (4): Persistent cache
  • LAZY (6): Load on demand
  • EAGER (7): Load immediately

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Language Agnostic: Support any runtime/language
  2. Progressive Extraction: Load only what's needed
  3. Secure by Default: Always verify signatures
  4. Zero Dependencies: Static, portable launchers
  5. Cross-Platform: Linux, macOS, Windows support
  6. Reproducible: Deterministic builds
  7. Testable: Comprehensive test coverage

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: Can I distribute unsigned packages? A: Yes, but users must set FLAVOR_INSECURE=1 to run them. Not recommended for production.

Q: How do I update a package? A: Rebuild with new version in pyproject.toml. Old workenv caches are automatically replaced.

Q: Can I embed secrets in a package? A: No. Packages are not encrypted. Use environment variables or external config files for secrets.

Q: Why is my package so large? A: Python runtime is embedded. Use --strip flag and ensure unnecessary files are excluded.

Q: Can I use system Python instead of embedded? A: No. Packages are self-contained by design for portability.

docs.title: PSPF Format Overview
docs.text: The Progressive Secure Package Format (PSPF) 2025 Edition is a binary format for self-contained executable packages.

docs.title: Binary Structure
docs.text:
According to FEP-0001, a PSPF package has this exact structure:

Offset    Size      Component
--------  --------  ---------
0         Variable  Native Launcher Binary
L         Variable  Metadata Block (gzipped JSON)
M         Variable  Slot Table
S         Variable  Slot Data (0 to N slots)
EOF-8200  8200      Magic Trailer

docs.title: Magic Trailer (8200 bytes)
docs.text:
The last 8200 bytes of every PSPF file:

Offset    Size  Component
--------  ----  ---------
EOF-8200  4     Package emoji (📦) = [0xF0, 0x9F, 0x93, 0xA6]
EOF-8196  8192  Index Block
EOF-4     4     Magic wand emoji (🪄) = [0xF0, 0x9F, 0xAA, 0x84]

docs.title: Index Block (8192 bytes)
docs.text: Located at EOF-8196, contains critical offsets and metadata:

docs.title: Key Fields (from offset 0):
docs.text:
• 0-3: Format version (0x20250001)
  • 4-7: Index checksum (Adler-32)
  • 8-15: Package size
  • 16-23: Launcher size
  • 24-31: Metadata offset
  • 32-39: Metadata size
  • 40-47: Slot table offset
  • 48-55: Slot table size
  • 56-59: Slot count
  • 60-63: Flags
  • 64-95: Ed25519 public key
  • 96-127: Metadata checksum (SHA-256)
  • 128-639: Signature and other fields
  • 640-1375: Extended fields
  • 1376-8191: Reserved (zero-filled)

docs.title: Slot System
docs.text: Slots are numbered containers (0-based) for application data.

docs.title: Slot Table Entry (64 bytes each):
docs.text:
Offset  Size  Field           Description
------  ----  --------------  -----------
0       4     id              Slot number
4       8     offset          Offset in package
12      8     size            Compressed size
20      8     original_size   Uncompressed size
28      4     checksum        Adler-32
32      1     encoding        Encoding type
33      1     purpose         Purpose type
34      1     lifecycle       Lifecycle type
35      1     flags           Slot flags
36-63   28    (various)       Additional fields

docs.title: Encoding Types:
docs.text:
• 0: RAW (uncompressed)
  • 1: TAR (tar archive)
  • 2: GZIP (gzipped)
  • 3: TGZ (tar then gzip)

docs.title: Purpose Types:
docs.text:
• 0: DATA (general data)
  • 1: CODE (executable code)
  • 2: CONFIG (configuration)
  • 3: MEDIA (assets)

docs.title: Lifecycle Types:
docs.text:
• 0: INIT (first run only)
  • 1: STARTUP (every startup)
  • 2: RUNTIME (normal extraction)
  • 3: SHUTDOWN (at termination)
  • 4: CACHE (cacheable)
  • 5: TEMPORARY (session only)
  • 6: LAZY (load on demand)
  • 7: EAGER (load immediately)
  • 8: DEV (development only)
  • 9: CONFIG (user-modifiable)
  • 10: PLATFORM (platform-specific)

docs.title: Metadata Format
docs.text:
Stored as gzipped JSON at the offset specified in the index:

{
  "package": {
    "name": "package-name",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  },
  "slots": [
    {
      "id": 0,
      "name": "runtime",
      "size": 38000000,
      "encoding": 3,
      "purpose": 1,
      "lifecycle": 2
    }
  ],
  "execution": {
    "command": "python",
    "args": ["-m", "app"],
    "primary_slot": 0
  }
}

docs.title: Signature Verification
docs.text: Packages are signed with Ed25519: 1. The integrity_signature field (128-639 in index) contains the signature 2. Signature covers the index block (with signature zeroed) and metadata 3. Public key is stored at bytes 64-95 of the index

docs.title: Implementation Requirements
docs.text: Per the specification, implementations MUST: - Verify the magic footer bytes exactly - Validate all checksums (index, metadata, slots) - Begin major sections on 8-byte boundaries - Use little-endian byte order - Prevent path traversal attacks

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Launchers set these variables: - FLAVOR_WORKENV: Workenv directory path - FLAVOR_PACKAGE_NAME: Package name - FLAVOR_PACKAGE_VERSION: Package version - FLAVOR_SLOT_{N}_PATH: Path to extracted slot N

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Signatures verified by default (unless FLAVOR_INSECURE=1)
  • All checksums must be validated
  • Path traversal prevented during extraction

For the complete specification, see FEP-0001.

docs.title: 1. Create a Simple Python Application
docs.text:
Create hello.py: 

#!/usr/bin/env python3

def main():
    print("Hello from FlavorPack!")
    print("Running from a PSPF package")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: 2. Create Package Manifest
docs.text:
Create pyproject.toml: 

[project]
name = "hello"
version = "1.0.0"
description = "My first PSPF package"
requires-python = ">=3.11"

[project.scripts]
hello = "hello:main"

[tool.flavor]
entry_point = "hello:main"

docs.title: 3. Build the Package
docs.text:
# Create PSPF package
flavor pack --manifest pyproject.toml --output hello.psp

# The package will contain:
# - Native launcher (Go or Rust)
# - 8192-byte index block with metadata
# - Python runtime (slot 0)
# - Your application (slot 1)
# - Magic trailer (📦 + index + 🪄)

docs.title: 4. Run Your Package
docs.text:
# Make executable
chmod +x hello.psp

# Run it
./hello.psp

docs.title: Understanding the Package Structure
docs.text:
According to the PSPF/2025 specification, your package contains:

Offset    Size      Component
--------  --------  ---------
0         Variable  Native Launcher Binary
L         Variable  Metadata Block (gzipped JSON)
M         Variable  Slot Table
S         Variable  Slot Data (0 to N slots)
EOF-8200  8200      Magic Trailer

The Magic Trailer (last 8200 bytes): 

EOF-8200  4     Package emoji (📦) [0xF0 0x9F 0x93 0xA6]
EOF-8196  8192  Index Block
EOF-4     4     Magic wand emoji (🪄) [0xF0 0x9F 0xAA 0x84]

docs.title: Verify Package
docs.text:
# Verify integrity and signature
flavor verify hello.psp

docs.title: Inspect Package
docs.text:
# View package metadata and structure
flavor inspect hello.psp

docs.title: Extract Package
docs.text:
# Extract contents for inspection
flavor extract hello.psp --output extracted/

docs.title: Working Environment
docs.text: Packages extract to a cache directory: - Linux: ~/.cache/flavor/workenv/{name}_{version} - macOS: ~/Library/Caches/flavor/workenv/{name}_{version} - Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\flavor\workenv\{name}_{version}

docs.title: FEP-0001: Progressive Secure Package Format (PSPF/2025) Core Specification
docs.text: Status: Implemented Type: Standards Track Created: 2025-08-28 Updated: 2025-09-02

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: This specification defines the Progressive Secure Package Format (PSPF), version 2025, a binary format for self-contained executable packages. PSPF packages combine a native launcher executable with compressed application data into a single file that functions as both an operating system executable and a structured archive.

docs.title: 1.1. Requirements Language
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

docs.title: 1.2. Design Goals
docs.text:
1. Single-file distribution without external dependencies
  2. Cryptographic integrity verification
  3. Cross-platform execution (Linux, macOS, Windows)
  4. Progressive extraction with persistent caching
  5. Language-agnostic format suitable for any runtime

docs.title: 2. Binary Format Structure
docs.text:
A PSPF package consists of the following components in strict sequential order:

Offset    Size      Component
--------  --------  ---------
0         Variable  Native Launcher Binary
L         Variable  Metadata Block (gzipped JSON)
M         Variable  Slot Table
S         Variable  Slot Data (0 to N slots)
EOF-8200  8200      Magic Trailer (📦 + Index + 🪄)

The Magic Trailer (last 8200 bytes) contains: 

Offset    Size  Component
--------  ----  ---------
EOF-8200  4     Package emoji (📦)
EOF-8196  8192  Index Block
EOF-4     4     Magic wand emoji (🪄)

Where: - L = launcher_size (stored in index at EOF-8196) - M = metadata_offset (stored in index) - S = slot_table_offset (stored in index)

docs.title: 2.1. Byte Order
docs.text: All multi-byte integer values SHALL be stored in little-endian byte order.

docs.title: 2.2. Alignment
docs.text: All major sections SHALL begin on 8-byte boundaries. Padding bytes between sections SHALL be zero-filled.

docs.title: 3. Index Block Specification
docs.text: The index block is exactly 8192 bytes located at EOF-8196 (within the Magic Trailer).

docs.title: 3.1. Index Structure
docs.text:
Offset  Size  Type      Field                   Description
------  ----  --------  ----------------------  -----------
0       4     uint32    format_version          0x20250001
4       4     uint32    index_checksum          Adler-32 of bytes 0,8-8191
8       8     uint64    package_size            Total file size in bytes
16      8     uint64    launcher_size           Size of launcher executable
24      8     uint64    metadata_offset         Offset to metadata block
32      8     uint64    metadata_size           Size of compressed metadata
40      8     uint64    slot_table_offset       Offset to slot table
48      8     uint64    slot_table_size         Size of slot table
56      4     uint32    slot_count              Number of slots (0-65535)
60      4     uint32    flags                   Package flags (see 3.2)
64      32    bytes     public_key              Ed25519 public key
96      32    bytes     metadata_checksum       SHA-256 of metadata
128     512   bytes     integrity_signature     Signature data (see 3.3)
640     1     uint8     access_mode             Memory access hint
641     1     uint8     cache_strategy          Cache priority hint
642     1     uint8     encoding_type           Default encoding
643     1     uint8     encryption_type         Encryption (0=none)
644     4     uint32    page_size               Optimal page size
648     8     uint64    max_memory              Maximum memory needed
656     8     uint64    min_memory              Minimum memory needed
664     8     uint64    cpu_features            Required CPU features
672     8     uint64    gpu_requirements        GPU requirements
680     8     uint64    numa_hints              NUMA topology hints
688     4     uint32    stream_chunk_size       Streaming chunk size
692     12    bytes     padding1                Zero padding
704     8     uint64    build_timestamp         Unix timestamp
712     32    bytes     build_machine           Build host identifier
744     32    bytes     source_hash             Source code hash
776     32    bytes     dependency_hash         Dependencies hash
808     16    bytes     license_id              License identifier
824     8     uint64    provenance_uri_offset   URI offset (0=none)
832     8     uint64    capabilities            Capability flags
840     8     uint64    requirements            Requirement flags
848     8     uint64    extensions              Extension flags
856     4     uint32    compatibility           Compatibility version
860     4     uint32    protocol_version        Protocol version
864     512   bytes     future_crypto           Reserved for PQ crypto
1376    6816  bytes     reserved                Zero-filled

docs.title: 3.2. Flag Definitions
docs.text:
Bit  Name                Description
---  ------------------  -----------
0    SIGNED              Package has valid signature
1    COMPRESSED_INDEX    Index uses compression (future)
2    ENCRYPTED_SLOTS     Slots are encrypted (future)
3    STREAMING_READY     Optimized for streaming
4    DELTA_UPDATE        Supports delta updates (future)
5-31 Reserved            Must be zero

docs.title: 3.3. Checksum Calculation
docs.text:
The index_checksum field (offset 4-7) contains the Adler-32 checksum of the index block with the checksum field itself set to zero. Implementations MUST:

  1. Copy the index block to a buffer
  2. Set bytes 4-7 to zero
  3. Calculate Adler-32 of the entire 8192-byte buffer
  4. Compare with the stored checksum

docs.title: 3.4. Signature Verification
docs.text:
The integrity_signature field contains cryptographic signature data. The first 64 bytes contain an Ed25519 signature of: - The entire index block with signature field zeroed - The uncompressed metadata

Implementations SHOULD verify signatures unless explicitly disabled.

docs.title: 4. Metadata Specification
docs.text: Metadata is stored as gzip-compressed JSON at the offset specified in the index.

docs.title: 4.1. Required Fields
docs.text:
{
  "package": {
    "name": "STRING",        
    "version": "STRING"      
  },
  "slots": [
    {
      "id": INTEGER,         
      "name": "STRING",      
      "size": INTEGER,       
      "encoding": INTEGER,   
      "purpose": INTEGER,    
      "lifecycle": INTEGER   
    }
  ],
  "execution": {
    "command": "STRING",     
    "args": ["STRING"],      
    "primary_slot": INTEGER  
  }
}

docs.title: 4.2. Optional Fields
docs.text:
{
  "package": {
    "description": "STRING",
    "author": "STRING",
    "license": "STRING"
  },
  "workenv": {
    "directories": [
      {
        "path": "STRING",
        "mode": "STRING",
        "description": "STRING"
      }
    ],
    "env": {
      "KEY": "VALUE"
    }
  },
  "runtime": {
    "min_version": "STRING",
    "platform": "STRING"
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Slot System
docs.text: Slots are numbered containers (0-based) that hold application data.

docs.title: 5.1. Slot Table Entry (64 bytes)
docs.text:
Offset  Size  Type      Field             Description
------  ----  --------  ----------------  -----------
0       4     uint32    id                Slot number
4       8     uint64    offset            Offset in package
12      8     uint64    size              Compressed size
20      8     uint64    original_size     Uncompressed size
28      4     uint32    checksum          Adler-32 checksum
32      1     uint8     encoding          Encoding type
33      1     uint8     purpose           Purpose type
34      1     uint8     lifecycle         Lifecycle type
35      1     uint8     flags             Slot flags
36      8     uint64    name_hash         Hash of name
44      2     uint16    permissions       Unix permissions
46      18    bytes     reserved          Zero-filled

docs.title: 5.2. Encoding Types
docs.text:
Value  Name           Description
-----  -------------  -----------
0      RAW            Uncompressed data
1      TAR            TAR archive
2      GZIP           Gzip compressed
3      TGZ            TAR then gzip

docs.title: 5.3. Purpose Types
docs.text:
Value  Name           Description
-----  -------------  -----------
0      DATA           General data files
1      CODE           Executable code
2      CONFIG         Configuration
3      MEDIA          Media/assets

docs.title: 5.4. Lifecycle Types
docs.text:
Value  Name           Description
-----  -------------  -----------
0      INIT           First run only
1      STARTUP        Every startup
2      RUNTIME        Normal extraction
3      SHUTDOWN       At termination
4      CACHE          Cacheable
5      TEMPORARY      Session only
6      LAZY           Load on demand
7      EAGER          Load immediately
8      DEV            Development only
9      CONFIG         User-modifiable
10     PLATFORM       Platform-specific

docs.title: 6. Magic Footer
docs.text:
The last 8 bytes of the file contain UTF-8 encoded emoji characters serving as a unique identifier:

Offset  Size  Bytes              Character  Description
------  ----  -----------------  ---------  -----------
EOF-8   4     F0 9F 93 A6        📦         Package emoji
EOF-4   4     F0 9F AA 84        🪄         Magic wand emoji

Implementations MUST verify these bytes match exactly.

docs.title: 7.1. Launch Sequence
docs.text:
1. Read and verify magic footer
  2. Locate and read index block
  3. Verify index checksum
  4. Read and decompress metadata
  5. Verify metadata checksum
  6. Optionally verify signature
  7. Extract required slots to workenv
  8. Execute primary command

docs.title: 7.2. Working Environment
docs.text:
The working environment (workenv) is a directory where slots are extracted:

Platform  Environment Variable  Default Path
--------  -------------------  ------------
Linux     XDG_CACHE_HOME       ~/.cache/flavor/workenv/{name}_{version}
macOS     XDG_CACHE_HOME       ~/Library/Caches/flavor/workenv/{name}_{version}
Windows   LOCALAPPDATA         %LOCALAPPDATA%\flavor\workenv\{name}_{version}

docs.title: 7.3. Environment Variables
docs.text:
Launchers MUST set: - FLAVOR_WORKENV: Absolute path to workenv directory - FLAVOR_PACKAGE_NAME: Package name from metadata - FLAVOR_PACKAGE_VERSION: Package version from metadata

Launchers SHOULD set: - FLAVOR_SLOT_{N}_PATH: Path to extracted slot N - FLAVOR_OS: Operating system (linux/darwin/windows) - FLAVOR_ARCH: Architecture (amd64/arm64/x86)

docs.title: 8.1. Signature Verification
docs.text: Implementations MUST verify signatures by default unless: - The environment variable FLAVOR_INSECURE=1 is set - The implementation is explicitly configured to skip verification

docs.title: 8.2. Checksum Validation
docs.text: All checksums MUST be verified: - Index checksum before processing - Metadata checksum after decompression - Slot checksums after extraction

docs.title: 8.3. Path Traversal
docs.text: Implementations MUST prevent path traversal attacks when extracting slots. Paths containing .. or absolute paths MUST be rejected.

docs.title: 9.1. Minimum Implementation
docs.text: A conforming implementation MUST: - Read and verify the magic footer - Parse the index block - Verify index and metadata checksums - Extract at least one slot - Execute the specified command

docs.title: 9.2. Recommended Implementation
docs.text: Implementations SHOULD: - Verify Ed25519 signatures - Support all encoding types - Implement workenv caching - Support incremental extraction - Provide progress reporting

docs.title: 10. References
docs.text:
• RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs
  • RFC 1950: ZLIB Compressed Data Format
  • RFC 1952: GZIP file format
  • Ed25519: High-speed high-security signatures
  • Adler-32: Checksum algorithm

docs.title: FEP-0002: Working Environment Management Specification
docs.text: Status: Implemented Type: Standards Track Created: 2025-08-28 Updated: 2025-09-03

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: This specification defines the Working Environment (workenv) management system for PSPF/2025 packages. The workenv provides a persistent extraction cache with cryptographic validation, atomic operations, and lifecycle-based resource management.

docs.title: 1.1. Requirements Language
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

docs.title: 1.2. Design Goals
docs.text:
1. Persistent caching with cryptographic validation
  2. Atomic extraction preventing corruption from concurrent access
  3. Platform-agnostic directory structure
  4. Lifecycle-based automatic resource cleanup
  5. Deterministic path resolution through placeholder expansion

docs.title: 2.1. Base Path Resolution
docs.text:
The workenv base directory SHALL be determined using the following platform-specific algorithm:

Platform  Priority Order
--------  --------------
Linux     1. $XDG_CACHE_HOME/flavor/workenv/
          2. $HOME/.cache/flavor/workenv/

macOS     1. $XDG_CACHE_HOME/flavor/workenv/
          2. $HOME/Library/Caches/flavor/workenv/

Windows   1. %LOCALAPPDATA%\flavor\workenv\
          2. %APPDATA%\flavor\workenv\

docs.title: 2.2. Package Directory Structure
docs.text:
Each package SHALL have its own directory named {package_name}_{package_version}:

{base_path}/{package_name}_{package_version}/
├── .lock           # Process lock file (8 bytes)
├── .complete       # Extraction marker (0 bytes)
├── .manifest       # Cached metadata (JSON)
├── slot_0/         # Extracted slot 0
├── slot_1/         # Extracted slot 1
├── slot_N/         # Extracted slot N
└── {custom}/       # Package-defined directories

docs.title: 2.3. Lock File Format
docs.text:
The .lock file SHALL contain an 8-byte process identifier:

Offset  Size  Type     Description
------  ----  -------  -----------
0       4     uint32   Process ID (PID)
4       4     uint32   Unix timestamp

docs.title: 3.1. Validation Sequence
docs.text:
Implementations MUST validate cached content before use:

  1. Verify .complete marker exists
  2. Compare cached .manifest with package metadata
  3. Verify slot checksums if present
  4. Execute custom validation if specified

docs.title: 3.2. Completion Marker
docs.text:
The .complete file is a zero-byte file that MUST be created atomically after successful extraction:

  1. Extract all required slots
  2. Sync filesystem buffers
  3. Create .complete atomically
  4. Release lock

docs.title: 3.3. Custom Validation
docs.text:
Packages MAY specify custom validation in metadata:

{
  "workenv": {
    "cache_validation": {
      "check_file": "{workenv}/version.txt",
      "expected_content": "1.0.0",
      "checksum": "sha256:abcd1234..."
    }
  }
}

Implementations SHALL: 1. Expand placeholders in check_file 2. Read file content 3. Compare with expected_content or verify checksum 4. Invalidate cache on mismatch

docs.title: 4.1. Lock Acquisition
docs.text:
Implementations MUST use file-based locking:

  1. Open .lock with exclusive write access
  2. Write PID and timestamp
  3. Verify lock ownership
  4. Proceed with extraction
  5. Release lock on completion or failure

docs.title: 4.2. Lock Recovery
docs.text:
If lock acquisition fails:

  1. Read lock file content
  2. Check if owning process exists
  3. If process dead AND timestamp > 300 seconds old:
  4. Break lock and proceed
  5. Otherwise:
  6. Wait with exponential backoff
  7. Maximum wait time: 30 seconds

docs.title: 4.3. Partial Extraction Recovery
docs.text:
If .complete marker missing but partial content exists:

  1. Acquire exclusive lock
  2. Remove all existing content
  3. Perform fresh extraction
  4. Create .complete marker
  5. Release lock

docs.title: 5.1. Standard Placeholders
docs.text:
Implementations MUST support these placeholders:

Placeholder      Description                      Example Value
--------------   ------------------------------   -------------
{workenv}        Workenv directory path          /REDACTED_ABS_PATH
{home}           User home directory              /home/user
{tmp}            System temp directory            /tmp
{package}        Package name from metadata       myapp
{version}        Package version from metadata    1.0.0
{platform}       Platform identifier              linux_amd64
{slot_N}         Path to extracted slot N         /REDACTED_ABS_PATH

docs.title: 5.2. Expansion Rules
docs.text:
1. Placeholders SHALL be case-sensitive
  2. Unknown placeholders SHALL remain unexpanded
  3. Nested placeholders are NOT supported
  4. Expansion SHALL occur before path operations

docs.title: 5.3. Platform Identifiers
docs.text:
Platform identifiers SHALL use the format {os}_{arch}:

OS        Arch      Identifier
--------  --------  -----------
linux     amd64     linux_amd64
linux     arm64     linux_arm64
darwin    amd64     darwin_amd64
darwin    arm64     darwin_arm64
windows   amd64     windows_amd64

docs.title: 6.1. Metadata Specification
docs.text:
Packages MAY declare required directories:

{
  "workenv": {
    "directories": [
      {
        "path": "var/log",
        "mode": 493,
        "description": "Log directory"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Where mode is the decimal representation of Unix permissions (0755 = 493).

docs.title: 6.2. Creation Protocol
docs.text:
1. Set process umask if specified
  2. For each directory:
  3. Create with parents
  4. Apply mode & ~umask
  5. Continue on existing
  6. Restore original umask

docs.title: 6.3. Security Requirements
docs.text: Implementations MUST: - Reject paths containing .. components - Reject absolute paths - Verify paths remain within workenv - Apply umask to all created directories

docs.title: 7.1. Required Variables
docs.text:
Launchers MUST set before execution:

Variable                  Description                   Example
----------------------    ---------------------------   -------
FLAVOR_WORKENV           Absolute path to workenv      /REDACTED_ABS_PATH
FLAVOR_PACKAGE_NAME      Package name from metadata    myapp
FLAVOR_PACKAGE_VERSION   Package version from metadata 1.0.0

docs.title: 7.2. Optional Variables
docs.text:
Launchers SHOULD set if applicable:

Variable                  Description                   Example
----------------------    ---------------------------   -------
FLAVOR_SLOT_{N}_PATH     Path to extracted slot N      /REDACTED_ABS_PATH
FLAVOR_OS                Operating system               linux
FLAVOR_ARCH              Architecture                   amd64
FLAVOR_CACHE_DIR         Cache base directory           /REDACTED_ABS_PATH

docs.title: 8.1. Slot Lifecycles
docs.text:
Slots SHALL be retained or removed based on lifecycle (from FEP-0001):

Value  Name        Retention Policy
-----  ----------  ----------------
0      INIT        Remove after first successful run
1      STARTUP     Extract every launch
2      RUNTIME     Standard caching
3      SHUTDOWN    Remove at termination
4      CACHE       Persistent caching
5      TEMPORARY   Remove at termination
6      LAZY        Extract on first access
7      EAGER       Extract immediately

docs.title: 8.2. Cleanup Protocol
docs.text: After successful execution: 1. Remove INIT slots if first run 2. Remove TEMPORARY slots 3. Remove SHUTDOWN slots 4. Update .manifest with cleanup timestamp

docs.title: 8.3. Cache Expiration
docs.text: Implementations MAY remove workenvs based on: - Age (last access time) - Size constraints - Explicit user request - Package uninstallation

docs.title: 9.1. Space Requirements
docs.text:
Before extraction, implementations SHOULD:

  1. Calculate total uncompressed size from metadata
  2. Add 20% overhead for filesystem metadata
  3. Verify available space
  4. Fail gracefully if insufficient

docs.title: 9.2. Quota Enforcement
docs.text:
Implementations MAY enforce quotas:

{
  "workenv": {
    "max_cache_size": 1073741824,
    "max_cache_age_days": 30
  }
}

docs.title: 10.1. Error Conditions
docs.text:
Implementations MUST handle:

  • Lock acquisition timeout
  • Insufficient disk space
  • Permission denied
  • Corrupted cache
  • Checksum mismatch

docs.title: 10.2. Recovery Actions
docs.text:
On error, implementations SHALL:

  1. Release any held locks
  2. Log error with context
  3. Attempt cache removal if corrupted
  4. Return specific error code
  5. NOT leave partial extractions

docs.title: 11.1. Path Traversal Prevention
docs.text: Implementations MUST validate all paths: - Reject .. components - Reject absolute paths - Canonicalize before operations - Verify within workenv boundaries

docs.title: 11.2. Permission Preservation
docs.text: Implementations SHOULD: - Preserve file permissions from slots - Apply umask consistently - Restrict workenv to user access only (0700)

docs.title: 11.3. Lock File Security
docs.text: Lock files MUST be: - Created with 0600 permissions - Verified for ownership - Protected from symbolic link attacks

docs.title: 12.1. Minimum Implementation
docs.text: A conforming implementation MUST: - Create workenv directory structure - Implement file-based locking - Support atomic extraction - Expand standard placeholders - Set required environment variables

docs.title: 12.2. Recommended Implementation
docs.text: Implementations SHOULD: - Validate cached content - Support lifecycle-based cleanup - Implement disk space checks - Provide cache management commands - Support custom validation

docs.title: 13. References
docs.text:
• RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs
  • FEP-0001: PSPF Core Specification
  • XDG Base Directory Specification
  • POSIX.1-2017: File locking

docs.title: FEP-0003: Runtime Security Model Specification
docs.text: Status: Partially Implemented Type: Standards Track Created: 2025-08-28 Updated: 2025-09-03

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: This specification defines the runtime security model for PSPF/2025 packages, establishing a four-layer environment processing system with declarative security policies for filesystem access, network restrictions, and resource limits.

docs.title: 1.1. Requirements Language
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

docs.title: 1.2. Security Objectives
docs.text:
1. Hermetic execution environment by default
  2. Explicit declaration of required host interactions
  3. Auditable security policy enforcement
  4. Defense against environment manipulation attacks
  5. Controlled privilege escalation prevention

docs.title: 2.1. Layer Processing Order
docs.text:
Environment variables SHALL be processed through four sequential layers:

Layer  Name        Function                Priority
-----  ----------  ----------------------  --------
0      Host        Inherited environment   Lowest
1      Security    Filter/block/map        Low
2      Workenv     Package-wide settings   Medium
3      Execution   Application-specific    High
4      Platform    System overrides        Highest

docs.title: 2.2. Layer Precedence Rules
docs.text:
1. Each layer MAY modify the environment from previous layers
  2. Later layers SHALL override earlier layers for conflicting keys
  3. Platform layer variables SHALL NOT be overridable
  4. Security layer SHALL have veto power through blocklists

docs.title: 3.1. Configuration Structure
docs.text:
The security layer configuration in metadata:

{
  "runtime": {
    "inherit_env": false,
    "env_passthrough": ["pattern1", "pattern2"],
    "env_blocklist": ["pattern3", "pattern4"],
    "env_mapping": {"HOST_KEY": "NEW_KEY"}
  }
}

docs.title: 3.2. Processing Algorithm
docs.text:
Implementations SHALL apply the following algorithm:

  1. Initialize: Start with empty environment unless inherit_env is true
  2. Passthrough: Add matching host variables from env_passthrough patterns
  3. Blocklist: Remove variables matching env_blocklist patterns
  4. Mapping: Rename variables according to env_mapping

docs.title: 3.3. Pattern Matching
docs.text: Patterns SHALL support: - Literal strings: HOME matches exactly HOME - Wildcards: LC_* matches LC_ALL, LC_TIME, etc. - Character classes: [A-Z]* matches variables starting with uppercase

docs.title: 3.4. Default Passthrough
docs.text:
If no env_passthrough specified, implementations SHOULD default to:

PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, TERM, LANG, LC_*, TZ

docs.title: 3.5. Mandatory Blocklist
docs.text:
Implementations SHALL always block (regardless of configuration):

LD_PRELOAD, LD_LIBRARY_PATH, DYLD_*, __CF_*

docs.title: 4.1. Configuration Structure
docs.text:
{
  "workenv": {
    "env": {
      "KEY": "value",
      "PATH_VAR": "{workenv}/bin:$PATH"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 4.2. Variable Expansion
docs.text: Values SHALL support: - Placeholder expansion (see FEP-0002 Section 5) - Reference to existing variables: $VAR or ${VAR} - Escape sequences: \$ for literal dollar sign

docs.title: 4.3. Processing Order
docs.text:
1. Expand placeholders
  2. Resolve variable references from current environment
  3. Set or override variables

docs.title: 5.1. Configuration Structure
docs.text:
{
  "execution": {
    "env": {
      "APP_KEY": "value"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 5.2. Scope
docs.text: Execution layer variables SHALL: - Apply only to the primary command execution - Override workenv layer variables - Support same expansion as workenv layer

docs.title: 6.1. Required Variables
docs.text:
Implementations MUST set:

Variable                Value Description              Example
----------------------  ----------------------------  -------
FLAVOR_WORKENV         Absolute path to workenv      /REDACTED_ABS_PATH
FLAVOR_PACKAGE_NAME    Package name from metadata    myapp
FLAVOR_PACKAGE_VERSION Package version from metadata 1.0.0
FLAVOR_OS              Operating system identifier   linux
FLAVOR_ARCH            Architecture identifier       amd64

docs.title: 6.2. Optional Variables
docs.text:
Implementations MAY set:

Variable                Value Description              Example
----------------------  ----------------------------  -------
FLAVOR_PLATFORM        Combined OS and arch          linux_amd64
FLAVOR_OS_VERSION      OS version string             5.15.0-91-generic
FLAVOR_CPU_TYPE        CPU type identifier           x86_64
FLAVOR_SLOT_{N}_PATH   Path to extracted slot N      /REDACTED_ABS_PATH

docs.title: 6.3. Override Protection
docs.text: Platform variables SHALL NOT be modifiable by: - Package metadata - User environment - Application code

docs.title: 7.1. Filesystem Access Control (Future)
docs.text:
When implemented, filesystem policies SHALL use:

{
  "security": {
    "filesystem": {
      "read_allowed": ["path_pattern"],
      "write_allowed": ["path_pattern"],
      "execute_allowed": ["path_pattern"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 7.2. Network Access Control (Future)
docs.text:
When implemented, network policies SHALL use:

{
  "security": {
    "network": {
      "allowed_hosts": ["hostname_pattern"],
      "allowed_ports": [port_numbers],
      "deny_local": boolean,
      "dns_servers": ["ip_addresses"]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 7.3. Resource Limits (Future)
docs.text:
When implemented, resource limits SHALL use:

{
  "security": {
    "resources": {
      "max_memory": bytes,
      "max_cpu": cores,
      "max_files": count,
      "max_processes": count
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 8.1. Activation
docs.text: Insecure mode SHALL be activated when environment variable FLAVOR_INSECURE equals 1.

docs.title: 8.2. Effects
docs.text:
In insecure mode, implementations SHALL:

  1. Skip signature verification (see FEP-0001)
  2. Inherit full host environment
  3. Disable filesystem restrictions
  4. Disable network restrictions
  5. Log warning to stderr

docs.title: 8.3. Warning Format
docs.text:
The warning MUST be visible and include: 

WARNING: Running in INSECURE mode - signatures not verified, security policies disabled

docs.title: 9.1. Security Events
docs.text:
Implementations SHOULD log:

  • Environment variable filtering
  • Blocked filesystem operations
  • Blocked network connections
  • Resource limit violations
  • Insecure mode activation

docs.title: 9.2. Log Format
docs.text:
Security logs SHALL include:

{
  "timestamp": "ISO-8601",
  "level": "security",
  "event": "event_type",
  "details": {
    "action": "blocked|allowed|modified",
    "target": "resource_identifier",
    "policy": "policy_name"
  }
}

docs.title: 10.1. Currently Implemented
docs.text:
• Platform layer environment variables
  • Basic workenv/execution layer variables
  • Placeholder expansion in variables

docs.title: 10.2. Not Yet Implemented
docs.text:
• Security layer filtering/mapping
  • Environment blocklist enforcement
  • Insecure mode detection
  • Filesystem access control
  • Network access control
  • Resource limits enforcement
  • Audit logging

docs.title: 11.1. Attack Vectors
docs.text:
Implementations MUST defend against:

  1. Environment injection: Malicious variables from host
  2. Path manipulation: Altered PATH leading to wrong executables
  3. Library injection: LD_PRELOAD attacks
  4. Information disclosure: Leaking sensitive environment data
  5. Resource exhaustion: Unbounded resource consumption

docs.title: 11.2. Mitigation Strategies
docs.text:
1. Default deny for environment inheritance
  2. Explicit allowlisting required
  3. Mandatory blocklist for dangerous variables
  4. Platform variables non-overridable
  5. Audit trail for security events

docs.title: 11.3. Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use minimal env_passthrough lists
  2. Never pass through credential patterns
  3. Validate all user input before expansion
  4. Log security-relevant events
  5. Regular security policy review

docs.title: 12.1. Linux
docs.text:
• Consider SELinux/AppArmor profiles
  • Use seccomp for syscall filtering
  • Leverage cgroups for resource limits

docs.title: 12.2. macOS
docs.text:
• Use sandbox-exec for sandboxing
  • Consider Hardened Runtime
  • Leverage Endpoint Security framework

docs.title: 12.3. Windows
docs.text:
• Use AppContainer for isolation
  • Consider Windows Defender Application Control
  • Leverage Job Objects for resource limits

docs.text:
• RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs
  • FEP-0001: PSPF Core Specification
  • FEP-0002: Working Environment Management
  • POSIX.1-2017: Environment variables
  • Linux capabilities(7)

docs.title: FEP-0004: Staged Payload Architecture Specification
docs.text: Status: Proposed Type: Standards Track Created: 2025-08-28 Updated: 2025-09-03

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: This specification defines the Staged Payload Architecture (SPA), an optional extension to PSPF/2025 enabling concurrent execution of untrusted initialization code during cryptographic verification. SPA improves perceived startup performance through asynchronous "start-then-halt" verification while maintaining security guarantees.

docs.title: 1.1. Requirements Language
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

docs.title: 1.2. Design Goals
docs.text:
1. Reduce perceived startup latency without compromising security
  2. Execute non-sensitive initialization during verification
  3. Maintain clear trust boundaries between components
  4. Provide platform-agnostic sandboxing mechanisms
  5. Enable graceful degradation on failure

docs.title: 2.1. Component Structure
docs.text:
A SPA-enabled PSPF package contains:

Component               Trust Level    Execution Phase
---------------------   ------------   ---------------
Native Launcher         Trusted        Always
Verification Engine     Trusted        Concurrent
PVP (Slot 0)           Untrusted      Pre-verification
Main Application        Trusted        Post-verification

docs.title: 2.2. Execution Timeline
docs.text:
Time(ms): 0     50    100   150   200   250   300
          |-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|-----|
Verify:   [====Hashing====][Sig Check][Done]→
PVP:      [Init][UI][Cache]→[Wait----][Main→
                            ↑
                   Verification Boundary

docs.title: 2.3. Index Flag
docs.text:
SPA capability SHALL be indicated by bit 5 in the index flags field:

Bit  Name           Value    Description
---  -------------  -------  -----------
5    SPA_ENABLED    0x20     Package supports SPA

docs.title: 3.1. Designation
docs.text: The PVP SHALL be stored in slot 0 with lifecycle type 0 (INIT) and purpose type 1 (CODE).

docs.title: 3.2. Metadata Configuration
docs.text:
Packages SHALL declare SPA configuration in metadata:

{
  "spa": {
    "enabled": true,
    "pvp_slot": 0,
    "pvp_timeout_ms": 5000,
    "pvp_max_memory": 104857600,
    "pvp_capabilities": ["ui_render", "temp_files"],
    "boundary_type": "synchronous",
    "boundary_timeout_ms": 10000
  }
}

docs.title: 3.3. Capability Definitions
docs.text:
Capability    Description                 Allowed Operations
-----------   -------------------------   ------------------
ui_render     Display user interface      Window creation, drawing
temp_files    Temporary file access       Write to temp directory
ipc_setup     Inter-process communication Create IPC channels
cache_init    Initialize caches           Memory allocation
config_load   Load default configuration  Read embedded config

docs.title: 3.4. Restricted Operations
docs.text: PVP code SHALL NOT: - Access network interfaces - Read user files - Write to persistent storage - Execute external processes - Load dynamic libraries - Access cryptographic keys - Modify system configuration

docs.title: 4.1. Boundary Definition
docs.text: The Verification Boundary is a mandatory synchronization point where PVP execution halts until verification completes.

docs.title: 4.2. Signaling Mechanism
docs.text:
Implementations SHALL provide one of:

  1. Shared Memory: 4096-byte page with verification state
  2. Unix Socket: Domain socket at /tmp/pspf_{pid}.sock
  3. Named Pipe: Platform-specific pipe
  4. Semaphore: System V or POSIX semaphore

docs.title: 4.3. State Structure
docs.text:
The verification state SHALL contain:

Offset  Size  Type      Field               Description
------  ----  --------  ------------------  -----------
0       4     uint32    magic               0x53504156 ('SPAV')
4       4     uint32    version             Protocol version
8       4     uint32    state               0=pending, 1=verified, 2=failed
12      4     uint32    error_code          Error if failed
16      32    bytes     metadata_hash       SHA-256 of metadata
48      8     uint64    timestamp           Verification completion time
56      4040  bytes     reserved            Zero-filled

docs.title: 4.4. Handshake Protocol
docs.text:
PVP → Engine: READY(pid, nonce)
Engine → PVP: ACK(nonce)
PVP → Engine: AT_BOUNDARY
[Verification occurs]
Engine → PVP: VERIFIED(hash) | FAILED(error)
PVP → Engine: PROCEEDING | TERMINATING

docs.title: 5.1. Process Isolation
docs.text: PVP execution SHALL occur in a separate process with: - Restricted system call access - Limited file system visibility - No network capabilities - Bounded resource consumption

docs.title: 5.2. System Call Filtering
docs.text:
Implementations SHALL block at minimum:

Category        Blocked Calls
--------------  -------------
Network         socket, connect, bind, listen
Process         fork, execve, clone
Filesystem      mount, chroot, pivot_root
Kernel          module_load, reboot
Privilege       setuid, setgid, capset

docs.title: 5.3. Resource Limits
docs.text:
Resource        Limit           Enforcement
--------------  --------------  -----------
Memory          pvp_max_memory  Process limit
CPU Time        pvp_timeout_ms  Timer signal
File Handles    256             Resource limit
Threads         1               Clone prevention

docs.title: 6.1. Launcher Modifications
docs.text:
Launchers implementing SPA SHALL:

  1. Check SPA_ENABLED flag in index
  2. Parse SPA configuration from metadata
  3. Create verification state structure
  4. Spawn verification thread/process
  5. Spawn PVP executor with sandbox
  6. Synchronize at verification boundary
  7. Continue with main application or terminate

docs.title: 6.2. Verification Engine
docs.text:
The verification engine SHALL:

  1. Run independently of PVP execution
  2. Complete full cryptographic verification
  3. Signal result through agreed mechanism
  4. NOT be influenced by PVP execution

docs.title: 6.3. PVP Executor
docs.text:
The PVP executor SHALL:

  1. Extract and validate PVP slot
  2. Configure sandbox environment
  3. Execute PVP code with restrictions
  4. Block at verification boundary
  5. Terminate on timeout or failure

docs.title: 7.1. Failure Modes
docs.text:
Failure              Detection                Action
-------------------  ----------------------   ------
PVP timeout          Timer expiration         Kill PVP, continue verify
PVP crash            Process termination      Log, continue normally
Verification fail    Signature invalid        Kill PVP, terminate
Sandbox breach       Syscall violation        Kill PVP, terminate
Resource exceeded    Limit reached            Kill PVP, continue

docs.title: 7.2. Graceful Degradation
docs.text: On PVP failure, implementations SHALL: 1. Log the failure with details 2. Clean up PVP resources 3. Continue verification if not compromised 4. Launch without PVP benefits if verified

docs.title: 8.1. Trust Model
docs.text:
1. PVP code is ALWAYS untrusted before verification
  2. Verification engine MUST be isolated from PVP
  3. Sandbox escape SHALL terminate execution
  4. Resource exhaustion SHALL NOT affect verification

docs.title: 8.2. Attack Mitigation
docs.text:
Attack Vector         Mitigation
-------------------   -----------
Sandbox escape        Process isolation, syscall filtering
Resource exhaustion   Hard limits, timeout enforcement
Data exfiltration     No network access, limited I/O
Verification bypass   Complete isolation of verifier
Race conditions       Atomic operations, proper locking

docs.title: 8.3. Defense Layers
docs.text:
1. Process Isolation: Separate address space
  2. Syscall Filtering: Kernel-level enforcement
  3. Resource Capping: Hard limits on consumption
  4. Time Bounds: Mandatory timeout
  5. Capability Dropping: Minimal privileges
  6. Audit Logging: Complete operation trail

docs.title: 9.1. Linux
docs.text:
• Sandbox: seccomp-bpf, namespaces
  • IPC: Unix domain sockets, shared memory
  • Resources: cgroups, rlimits

docs.title: 9.2. macOS
docs.text:
• Sandbox: sandbox-exec profiles
  • IPC: Mach ports, Unix sockets
  • Resources: Sandbox resource limits

docs.title: 9.3. Windows
docs.text:
• Sandbox: AppContainer, Job Objects
  • IPC: Named pipes, shared memory
  • Resources: Job Object limits

docs.title: 10.1. Measurement Points
docs.text:
Implementations SHOULD track:

Metric                    Description                 Target
----------------------    -------------------------   ------
time_to_first_pixel       PVP UI display              <50ms
verification_duration     Signature verification      <500ms
boundary_wait_time        Time blocked at boundary    <10ms
total_startup_time        Launch to main execution    <600ms

docs.title: 10.2. Optimization Opportunities
docs.text:
1. Parallel hash computation during PVP execution
  2. Incremental signature verification
  3. Cached verification results
  4. Pre-computed sandbox configuration

docs.title: 11.1. FEP-0005 (JIT Loading)
docs.text: SPA and JIT Loading are complementary: - SPA handles pre-verification initialization - JIT handles post-verification lazy loading - Combined use reduces both perceived and actual startup time

docs.title: 11.2. FEP-0003 (Security Model)
docs.text: SPA respects the security model: - PVP runs with minimal environment - Security policies enforced post-verification - Insecure mode affects verification, not sandboxing

docs.title: 12. References
docs.text:
• RFC 2119: Key words for use in RFCs
  • FEP-0001: PSPF Core Specification
  • FEP-0003: Runtime Security Model
  • FEP-0005: Just-In-Time Loading
  • Linux seccomp(2)

docs.title: FEP-0005: Just-In-Time Loading Specification
docs.text: Status: Proposed Type: Standards Track Created: 2025-09-02 Updated: 2025-09-03

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: This specification defines Just-In-Time (JIT) loading mechanisms for PSPF/2025 packages, enabling deferred extraction of slots and on-demand network delivery. JIT loading reduces startup time, memory usage, and bandwidth consumption by loading components only when needed.

docs.title: 1.1. Requirements Language
docs.text: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

docs.title: 1.2. Design Goals
docs.text:
1. Minimize startup latency through deferred loading
  2. Reduce memory footprint via on-demand extraction
  3. Enable network-based component delivery
  4. Support incremental updates and patches
  5. Maintain cryptographic integrity for all content

docs.title: 2.1. Extended Lifecycle Types
docs.text:
In addition to FEP-0001 lifecycle types, JIT adds:

Value  Name            Description                     Loading
-----  --------------  ------------------------------  -------
11     JIT_LOCAL       Load from package on demand    Deferred
12     JIT_NETWORK     Load from network on demand    Network
13     JIT_HYBRID      Try local, fall back to network Mixed
14     JIT_OPTIONAL    Load only if explicitly used   Manual
15     JIT_BACKGROUND  Load in background after start Async

docs.title: 2.2. Loading Priority
docs.text:
Slots SHALL be loaded in priority order:

Priority  Lifecycle Types           When Loaded
--------  -----------------------   -----------
1         EAGER, STARTUP           Before main execution
2         RUNTIME                  At first access
3         JIT_LOCAL                On demand
4         JIT_BACKGROUND           After startup
5         JIT_NETWORK, JIT_HYBRID  When accessed
6         JIT_OPTIONAL             Explicit request only

docs.title: 3.1. JIT Configuration
docs.text:
Packages SHALL declare JIT configuration in metadata:

{
  "jit": {
    "enabled": true,
    "strategy": "aggressive",
    "cache_dir": "{workenv}/.jit_cache",
    "max_cache_size": 1073741824,
    "network_timeout_ms": 30000,
    "background_slots": [4, 5, 6]
  }
}

docs.title: 3.2. Slot-Level JIT Configuration
docs.text:
Each slot MAY specify JIT parameters:

{
  "slots": [
    {
      "id": 3,
      "name": "large-model",
      "lifecycle": 12,
      "jit": {
        "source": {
          "type": "grpc",
          "endpoint": "api.example.com:443",
          "path": "/slots/model-v2"
        },
        "cache": {
          "strategy": "persistent",
          "ttl": 86400,
          "verify_on_load": true
        },
        "priority": 5
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: 4.1. Deferred Extraction
docs.text:
For JIT_LOCAL slots, implementations SHALL:

  1. Skip extraction during initial workenv setup
  2. Track slot access through filesystem hooks
  3. Extract slot on first access
  4. Cache extraction for subsequent access

docs.title: 4.2. Access Detection Mechanisms
docs.text:
Implementations SHALL use one or more:

  1. Filesystem Hooks: Intercept file operations
  2. Import Hooks: Language-specific module loading
  3. Explicit API: Application requests loading
  4. Memory Mapping: Trap page faults for access

docs.title: 4.3. Extraction Protocol
docs.text: Access Detected → Check Cache → Extract if Missing → Verify Checksum → Grant Access

docs.title: 4.4. Cache Management
docs.text:
Extracted JIT slots SHALL be cached with:

Cache Key: {package_name}_{version}_{slot_id}_{checksum}
Cache Location: {workenv}/.jit_cache/slot_{id}/
Validation: Checksum verification on access
Expiration: LRU when cache_size exceeded

docs.title: 5.1. Network Source Types
docs.text:
Implementations MAY support:

Type      Protocol           Use Case
--------  -----------------  ---------
http      HTTP/HTTPS         Simple downloads
grpc      gRPC + Protobuf    Streaming, structured
s3        AWS S3 API         Cloud storage
webdav    WebDAV             Enterprise storage
custom    User-defined       Special requirements

docs.title: 5.2. Network Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "source": {
    "type": "grpc",
    "endpoint": "slots.example.com:443",
    "tls": true,
    "certificate_pin": "sha256:abcd1234..."
  },
  "auth": {
    "type": "bearer",
    "token": "${PSPF_TOKEN}"
  },
  "retry": {
    "max_attempts": 3,
    "backoff_ms": [1000, 2000, 4000]
  }
}

docs.title: 5.3. Download Protocol
docs.text:
1. Request: Send slot identifier and authentication
  2. Response: Receive slot size and checksum
  3. Transfer: Stream data in chunks
  4. Verification: Validate complete slot checksum
  5. Extraction: Decompress and extract to cache

docs.title: 5.4. Chunk Transfer
docs.text:
For streaming protocols, chunks SHALL include:

Offset  Size  Type      Field         Description
------  ----  --------  ------------  -----------
0       4     uint32    sequence      Chunk number
4       4     uint32    size          Data size
8       4     uint32    checksum      Chunk Adler-32
12      N     bytes     data          Chunk data

docs.title: 6.1. Service Definition
docs.text:
For gRPC-based delivery:

syntax = "proto3";

service SlotService {
  rpc GetSlotInfo(SlotRequest) returns (SlotInfo);
  rpc DownloadSlot(SlotRequest) returns (stream SlotChunk);
  rpc CheckUpdate(UpdateRequest) returns (UpdateInfo);
}

message SlotRequest {
  string package_id = 1;
  string package_version = 2;
  uint32 slot_id = 3;
  string auth_token = 4;
}

message SlotChunk {
  uint32 sequence = 1;
  bytes data = 2;
  uint32 checksum = 3;
  float progress = 4;
}

docs.title: 6.2. Authentication
docs.text:
Network requests SHALL include authentication:

Method        Header/Field           Example
-----------   --------------------   -------
HTTP Bearer   Authorization          Bearer {token}
gRPC Meta     authorization          bearer {token}
Custom Auth   X-PSPF-Auth           {signed_request}

docs.title: 7.1. Slot Verification
docs.text:
All JIT-loaded slots MUST be verified:

  1. Compare slot checksum with metadata
  2. Verify slot signature if present
  3. Validate internal structure
  4. Check file permissions

docs.title: 7.2. Network Security
docs.text:
Network delivery SHALL:

  1. Use TLS for all connections
  2. Verify server certificates
  3. Support certificate pinning
  4. Validate chunk checksums
  5. Verify complete slot integrity

docs.title: 7.3. Cache Validation
docs.text:
Cached slots SHALL be validated by:

On Access: Quick checksum of cache marker
Periodic: Full checksum verification
On Error: Complete re-validation
After Update: Invalidate affected slots

docs.title: 8.1. Prefetching
docs.text:
Implementations MAY prefetch based on:

  • Access patterns from previous runs
  • Static dependency analysis
  • Explicit prefetch hints
  • Background loading priority

docs.title: 8.2. Compression
docs.text:
Network transfers SHOULD use:

Protocol     Compression          Typical Ratio
----------   ------------------   -------------
HTTP         gzip, brotli         3-5x
gRPC         gzip, snappy         2-4x
Custom       zstd, lz4            2-10x

docs.title: 8.3. Caching Strategy
docs.text:
Strategy      Description                When to Use
-----------   -------------------------  -----------
Persistent    Keep indefinitely          Stable content
Temporal      Time-based expiration      Dynamic content
Size-bound    LRU with size limit        Limited storage
Versioned     Per-version caching        Frequent updates

docs.title: 9.1. Local JIT Failures
docs.text:
Failure              Recovery Action
------------------   ---------------
Extraction fails     Retry with verification
Checksum mismatch    Re-extract from package
No disk space        Clear cache, retry
Access timeout       Return error to application

docs.title: 9.2. Network JIT Failures
docs.text:
Failure              Recovery Action
------------------   ---------------
Connection failed    Retry with backoff
Server error         Try alternate endpoint
Partial download     Resume from offset
Verification fail    Full re-download
Auth expired         Refresh credentials

docs.title: 10.1. Minimum Implementation
docs.text:
A conforming implementation MUST:

  • Support JIT_LOCAL lifecycle
  • Implement basic cache management
  • Verify slot checksums
  • Handle extraction failures

docs.title: 10.2. Network Implementation
docs.text:
Network-capable implementations MUST:

  • Support at least HTTP(S)
  • Implement retry logic
  • Verify TLS certificates
  • Handle partial downloads
  • Validate all received data

docs.title: 10.3. Advanced Features
docs.text:
Implementations SHOULD support:

  • Multiple network protocols
  • Background prefetching
  • Compression for transfers
  • Incremental updates
  • Distributed caching

docs.title: 11.1. FEP-0004 (SPA)
docs.text: JIT Loading complements SPA: - SPA handles pre-verification UI - JIT handles post-verification loading - Combined: Fast perceived and actual startup

docs.title: 11.2. FEP-0002 (Workenv)
docs.text: JIT extends workenv management: - JIT cache within workenv - Shared cache across versions - Coordinated cleanup policies

docs.title: 12.1. Trust Model
docs.text:
1. Local JIT content is trusted (from verified package)
  2. Network content requires verification
  3. Cache corruption must be detected
  4. Network endpoints must be authenticated

docs.title: 12.2. Attack Mitigation
docs.text:
Attack                Mitigation
-------------------   -----------
Cache poisoning       Checksum verification
Network tampering     TLS + integrity checks
Denial of service     Timeouts + fallbacks
Path traversal        Sanitize slot paths
Resource exhaustion   Cache size limits
